Ceiling-Cassette Diffuser — Setpoint Comparison

12×10×4 m hall · two 4-way cassettes · identical airflow 1.81 m³/s · 14 °C supply · 12 kW load · buoyantPimpleFoam · matched snapshot at t = 350 s
Key finding. All three remove the same air mass and reach the same exit-air equilibrium (19.4 °C, 12 kW) by energy balance — they differ in how the air is used. The baseline mixes supply into the room, exhausts warm, and holds 24 °C with 89% comfort coverage. Swirl and steep short-circuit cold supply back to the return, so at a matched 350 s the room is 3–4 °C warmer, coverage collapses (swirl 4%), and they head toward a hotter, slower equilibrium.

ADPI caveat: ADPI is relative to the local mean, so swirl's uniformly-too-warm, calm zone scores highest ADPI (82) with the lowest real coverage (4%). Judge on absolute coverage + cooling removed.

Equilibrium (energy balance). At steady state the exhaust must satisfy Q = ṁ·cp·(T_exit − T_supply) → T_exit = 14 + 12000/(2.227·1004) = 19.4 °C for all three, removing the full 12 kW. The patterns differ only in how fast they get there and how hot the occupied zone sits meanwhile — baseline by ~185 s, swirl still climbing (31.5 °C at 806 s).

Room temperature vs time

Solid = occupied/volume mean, dotted = exit/return. Baseline flattens at setpoint by ~185 s; swirl and steep keep climbing toward hotter equilibria (very long time-constant — a thermostat or occupants would react long before).

Exit (return) flow — the mechanism

The exit temperature is the cooling delivered: Q = ṁ·cp·(T_exit − 14). Baseline exhausts warm (19 °C → 11.6 kW); swirl/steep exhaust cold (17 °C → ~8 kW) because cold supply short-circuits to the return.

Near-ceiling slice through the cassettes: in swirl/steep the blue (cold) air curls straight back into the central return; in baseline the returning air is warmer, having mixed with the room first.

Comfort coverage @1.1 m

Green = within comfort band (23–26 °C, V<0.35 m/s), red = outside. Baseline fills the plan; steep leaves gaps; swirl is almost entirely out of band at 350 s.

Model

OpenFOAM v2012 buoyantPimpleFoam (transient, compressible), k-ω SST, 576k cells, 4-core parallel. Hall 480 m³; two 0.6×0.6 m 4-way cassettes.

Controlled variable

Identical inlet area 0.64 m² and vertical supply −2.83 m/s → identical airflow 1.81 m³/s and mass flow 2.23 kg/s (mass conserved to ~1e-10). Only the horizontal throw direction differs.

Why the mean differs

Open system: dU/dt = Q − ṁ·cp·(T_exit − T_supply). Q, ṁ, T_supply identical, so the only difference is the exit temperature — set by the flow pattern. Lower exit T (short-circuit) → less heat carried out → warmer room.

Caveats

Matched snapshot at t = 350 s. Baseline is at steady state; swirl & steep are still approaching a hotter equilibrium (not force-converged). Single mesh (576k); RANS turbulence.
